stages.a: A slit cut across the long face of the block.
stages.v: Cut a slit or cross about 6 mm deep on the long face for a dense, large cluster.

stages.a: Cobweb-like mycelium puffs out of the cut, beaded with amber droplets.
stages.v: Cobweb fluff from the cut, amber droplets at about 5-7 days, then primordia. It is slower to pin than most oysters.

stages.a: Pins form on the puff at the cut.
stages.v: Black oysters can form puffs or mounds at cut sites with pins on them. Ideal 13-16 °C; above about 18 °C pinning drops steeply.

stages.a: Thick white stems rise in a tight cluster, carrying small dark caps.
stages.v: Cold-grown fruit look king-like, with thick stems, but clustered. Warm-grown fruit look more like blue oyster.

stages.a: The caps open dark and rounded, the edges still turned down.
stages.v: Pick before the caps flatten or over-expand: about 10-14 days from pins.

stages.a: The caps turn up and drop spores.
stages.v: A day late (caps upturning, spores dropping) visibly costs weight. Treat it as a one-flush strain.

labels.a: The slit on the long face of the block.
labels.v: About 6 mm deep on the long face.

labels.a: Aerial mycelium puffing out of the cut.
labels.v: Cobweb-like fluff comes first, then droplets, then primordia.

labels.a: Amber droplets beading on the fluff.
labels.v: Amber droplets appear at about 5-7 days.

labels.a: Pins on the mound at the cut.
labels.v: Puffs or mounds at the cut, with pins on them.

labels.a: Thick white stems, king-like but clustered.
labels.v: Exhaust at about 800-900 ppm CO2 keeps the stems from stretching.

labels.a: A young cap keeps its edge turned down.

labels.v: Fairly good shelf life if picked before the caps flatten.

labels.a: Gills run down from the cap onto the stem.
The cap edge turns up: a day late.
labels.v: Upturning caps and dropping spores visibly cost weight.

labels.a: Spores drift down from the gills.
